The very first Popsicle water ice was created way back in 1905 by an 11-year-old named Frank Epperson. That’s right, Popsicle was invented by a kid! After a long day of play, Frank went inside but left a fizzy drink with a stirring stick on the veranda. The night got cold, and when Frank went outside the next morning, he found his drink frozen like an icicle. Frank called his invention the ‘Epsicle’. It was a hit with the kids at school, and later with his own kids who called it ‘Pop’s sicle’, and that’s where Popsicle came from. The name was catchy and the treat was delicious, so Frank patented it in 1923 to share his Popsicle ice lollies with the world. name: La Gioiosa Prosecco Millesimato 75cl
description: La Gioiosa Prosecco Millesimato La Gioiosa is one of Italy's leading Prosecco producers. Based in Treviso in the heart of 'Prosecco country', La Gioiosa has consistently won awards across the globe and its quality wines are enjoyed my many. The winemaker freezes the Prosecco must prior to fermentation to ensure maximum freshness upon bottling. Its name pays tribute to the old definition of the province of Treviso, "Marca gioiosa et amorosa" (Joyous and Amorous March) underlining the sociable lifestyle of its inhabitants. Whole grapes are put into the pneumatic press for soft pressing and the resulting must, after a first racking, is put into controlled temperature tanks where it remains until it is used for the production of sparkling wine The must with added yeast cultures selected by La Gioiosa is then put into vessels where fermentation takes place at a controlled temperature of 15-16C to enhance all the harvest fragrances. Upon reaching the required alcohol and sugar content fermentation is stopped by refrigeration. name: Le Gall La Motte Churn Butter with Crystal Sea Salt 250g
description: Churn butter with crystal sea salt Le Gall butter is made in Finistère. Here, at the far western point of Brittany in France, cows can graze outside on fresh grass for a large part of the year, thanks to the mild climate of this coastal region Le Gall is proud to manufacture its butter following the traditional method for 100 years and their secret is to take their time to do things properly and obtain the best quality To ensure the best quality and the finest taste, this butter is made exclusively using fermented cream which will then be churned in drums. The cream used is exclusively from fresh milk. One of the particularities of Le Gall's butter is that the lactic starters used in the process are unique, carefully selected from the milk of their partners milk producers. They are selected and concentrated to obtain the best cultures with a stronger taste, typicity and above all a unique signature. This is then enhanced by the biological and physical maturation of the cream after the addition of the starters to give time for all the flavours and aromas to emerge and develop in the cream. The cream is then delicately churned in churning drums to avoid damaging the product and ensure the best texture The sea salt crystal used in this product also give unique qualities to it with a delicate salty flavour which slowly diffuse into your mouth added to a slightly crunchy texture The butter is 100% natural, no artificial colouring, flavouring, preservatives, or additives Le Gall Master Buttermaker explains that while manufacturing this butter, they use their senses to guide them during each production stage: they listen to the sound that the butter makes in the churn, they smell how it is developing, they see when it is ready, they seize the moment when its appearance and colour is just right, they touch it to make sure it has the right texture and they taste it to determine how successful the butter is This is why Le Gall's butter has this characteristic butter taste which will bring back childhood memories of the fresh butter directly made in farms Did you know that butter is the only fat that naturally contains Vitamin A and then 20g of butter provides 20% of your recommended daily intake of Vitamin A which contributes to better eyesight, growth and helps fight infection a well as improving the skin You can use Le Gall's butter to also create your own butter and brings originality to your dishes. Do it for them. (Do it for Carly.) Everyone has a Spirit Animal Ours is the wild mountain gout. It tells us to forage for fruit & veg in places they grow best. To always source our ingredients in a way that's good to the planet. And to grow beards that make others envious. So, we've done just that. It also tells us to wrap this up so you can get on and drink this delicious juice. You goat it An innocent guide to Befriending Fruit & Veg 1 Go for a drink with them, reveal too much 2 Have a deep, meaningful chinwag, find out you're both Libras born in the moon of Taurus 3 Become running buddies, realise you can't talk and run 4 Pay them a visit, have a nose around their home We visit our fruit and veg from time to time to make sure they're being grown in a way that's kind to the planet and everyone on it. We also check the people growing them are working in a safe place. And if something doesn't seem right, we do our best to sort it out. Because, well, that's what friends are for Our Favourite Bs Bees, border collies, bananas Blue is also one of our favourite Bs Who knew it? Lots of great things start with a B. And lately, our favourite one is the B Corp seal of approval. This recognises all the good stuff we've always done as a business. Like sourcing fruit & veg the right way and giving 10% of our profits to charity. B-rilliant Back for Good Boomerangs. Lost property The memory of last night's office party. name: Mr Johnsons Natural Oyster Shell Grit 1kg - Pack of 6
description: Mr. Johnsons Natural Oyster Shell Grit is a trusted and essential dietary supplement for domestic birds. This exceptional product consists of finely crushed oyster shells, meticulously sourced and processed to guarantee its quality and effectiveness. Oyster shell grit, also known as soluble grit, plays a crucial role in supporting the health and well-being of pet birds One of the standout features of this grit is its ability to dissolve within the bird"s digestive system. As birds ingest it, it gradually breaks down, releasing calcium into their bodies.
